record.paper_title: Some open problems on Banach spaces
record.original_question: Let E be a Kothe Banach space on [0,1], meaning a Banach space E contained in L^1[0,1] with 1_[0,1] in E and the lattice ideal property that |x| <= |y| with y in E implies x in E and ||x|| <= ||y||, and let X be a Banach space. Must every l2-strictly singular bounded linear operator T:E -> X be narrow, where l2-strictly singular means that the restriction of T to any subspace of E isomorphic to l2 is not an into-isomorphism?

evidence.quote: By a K¨othe Banach space on [0, 1] we mean a Banach space E ⊆ L1, 1[0,1] ∈ E and for each x ∈ L1 and y ∈ E the condition |x| ≤ |y| implies x ∈ E and kxk ≤ kyk.
Z-strictly singular if Z is an infinite dimensional Banach space, and the restriction T|Y of T to any subspace Y of E isomorphic to Z is not an into-isomorphism.
Problem 8.2. Is every `2-strictly singular operator narrow?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. A Köthe Banach space on [0,1] is a Banach space E with E ⊆ L^1[0,1] such that the constant function 1_{[0,1]} belongs to E and such that, for every measurable x and every y ∈ E with |x| ≤ |y| almost everywhere, one has x ∈ E and ‖x‖_E ≤ ‖y‖_E.

Let E be a Köthe Banach space on [0,1] and let X be a Banach space. A bounded linear operator T : E → X is called narrow if for every measurable set A ⊆ [0,1] and every ε > 0 there exists a function x ∈ E with x = -x on A (i.e. x takes only two opposite values on A and vanishes off A; equivalently, a "sign" of mean zero supported on A: x = 1_{A_1} − 1_{A_2} with A_1, A_2 disjoint and A_1 ∪ A_2 = A) such that ‖T(x)‖ < ε.

A bounded linear operator T : E → X is called ℓ_2-strictly singular if there is no closed infinite-dimensional subspace Y ⊆ E which is isomorphic to ℓ_2 and on which T acts as an into-isomorphism (i.e. there is no Y ⊆ E with Y ≃ ℓ_2 such that T|_Y is bounded below).

Question. Is it true that for every Köthe Banach space E on [0,1], every Banach space X, and every bounded linear operator T : E → X, if T is ℓ_2-strictly singular then T is narrow?
artifact.category_tag: narrow operators on Köthe Banach spaces
artifact.status_search_result: The general question (going back to Plichko–Popov, 1990) appears to still be open in full generality for arbitrary Köthe Banach spaces on [0,1]. Significant partial progress is known: Mykhaylyuk, Popov, Randrianantoanina, and Schechtman (Israel J. Math., 2014) proved that every ℓ_2-strictly singular operator from L_p (1 < p < ∞) to any Banach space with an unconditional basis is narrow. No source found that resolves the question for all Köthe Banach spaces.

status_evidence.title: Narrow and ℓ2-strictly singular operators from Lp
status_evidence.snippet: Every ℓ2-strictly singular operator from Lp, 1 < p < ∞, to any Banach space with an unconditional basis, is narrow, which partially answers a question of Plichko and Popov posed in 1990.
status_evidence.claim: The question is a long-standing problem of Plichko and Popov; only partial results are known.

status_evidence.title: NARROW AND ℓ2-STRICTLY SINGULAR OPERATORS FROM Lp
status_evidence.snippet: Partial answer to the question whether every ℓ2-strictly singular operator on Lp is narrow.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial answers are available; the general Köthe space case is not resolved in this work.
